label: early original-phase steps (t=1-4) after o/p/z/q-type prefixes, on a first-occurrence token from a favored set
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, almost entirely at t=1-5 (t=2 holds 44% of mass, t=3 31%). It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (19 of 64.6k activations). Within that window it depends on token identity in a graded way: it is stronger when earlier inputs include o, p, z, q (also a, f, n), e.g. first_tok o gives 3.2x lift, and when the current input is z, 0, c, o, f, e, n, t or j. It strongly prefers a token appearing for the first time (90% of mass). The largest activations come on z/0 right after an o- or p-initial prefix, e.g. o o z z or p p o z. The predicate is an additive proxy (a favored current token plus favored prior tokens, at least 2 hits) and captures about 68% of the mass at about 0.51 precision. The neuron looks like a distributed, token-weighted readout of the early prefix, not a clean category. The timing part alone (t=1-4) reaches 0.95 recall but only 0.16 precision.
